newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bank Santander takes major Argentina stake.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bank Santander takes major Argentina stake.

text.p: Leading Spanish bank Santander said on Tuesday it had bought control of Argentina's Banco Rio de la Plata, converting it into the nation's top private bank and reinforcing its leadership in the region.

In a statement, Santander said it would pay $594 million for 35.06 percent of Banco Rio's share capital with an option for an additional 15 percent. The initial stake provides voting control of the bank.
Santander will merge Banco Rio with its Banco Santander Argentina unit, creating the largest private bank in the country with assets in excess of $10 billion.

"Rio de la Plata is, in our opinion, the best banking franchise in the country with a magnificent tradition, financial strength, and excellent banking operations," Santander chairman Emilio Botin said in a statement.
"It is an agreement that fits perfectly with our retail banking strategy in Latin America and strengthens our presence as the leader in wholesale and pension funds in Argentina."

The purchase, at 2.6 times book value, brings Santander's investment in Latin America to $3.14 billion and its total assets in the region to $41.06 billion -- about double that of key Spanish rival Banco Bilbao Vizcaya .
"It's a good purchase, but I think it's expensive. BBV paid two times book value for Banco de Credito Argentino," a Madrid-based analyst said.
The acquisition follows recent purchases in Mexico, Colombia and Brazil.
"(The purchase) is at a higher multiple than we have been paying. But you have to pay a premium in Argentina. We think it's a good price for this bank," a Santander spokesman said.
Another analyst said that given a return on equity of 20 percent and a price-earnings ratio of 15, the price was fine.
"It doesn't seem very expensive...It's in line given the fierce competition between Santander and BBV," said, Beta Capital analyst Ignacio Cornejo.

Competition among Spanish banks has heated up dramatically in the region in the last year as they search for growth in the face of declining margins at home and worries of falling revenues under a common European currency.

Banco Rio has a $4.82 billion loan portfolio, giving it a market share of 6.9 percent. It has the lowest non-performing loan ratio among Argentine banks, standing at 3.04 percent with a provision coverage rate of 105 percent.
It has deposits totalling $3.59 billion, for a 6.2 percent market share.
